name: Question 1
problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
5{y}^{2}-y{e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y,\,y\ne 0.
$$
worked_solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

$$

$$

We have

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-y{e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y \\ -y{e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+5{y}^{2}-y & =0 \\ -y({e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-5y+1) & =0 \\ {e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-5y+1 & =0 \\ {e}^{x}({e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-5y+1) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-5y{e}^{x}+{e}^{x} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,+{{(-5{e}^{x})}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{-{e}^{x}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-5{e}^{x}y & =-{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=-5{e}^{x}$ and $Q(x)=-{e}^{x}.$

Question 1
?

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form. 5y2−ye−xdydx=y,y≠0.

a
 dydx+5y=−ex
b
 dydx−5xy=−e−x
c
dydx−5exy=x
d
dydx−5exy=−ex
e
dydx+5e−xy=e−x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as dydx+P(x)y=Q(x), where P(x) and Q(x) do not depend on y. We have 5y2−ye−xdydx=y−ye−xdydx+5y2−y=0−y(e−xdydx−5y+1)=0e−xdydx−5y+1=0ex(e−xdydx−5y+1)=0dydx−5yex+ex=0dydx+(−5ex)⏟P(x)y=−ex⏟Q(x)dydx−5exy=−ex Now, the equation is written in standard form with P(x)=−5ex and Q(x)=−ex.
